act_descr:
Act I)
  - Roma Norte, rainy season. Morada’s compressor dies mid-service; Ana pawns her knife roll for ice, patches a scorched plancha, juggles supplier threats and back rent. Mateo logs chaos on his phone. Carmen wanders from her clinic near Hospital General; a whiff of burnt piloncillo makes her hum boleros and ask for mole she can’t name.
  - Mikel Arriaga’s pending “promising but unfocused” review looms. Diego Ramos slides into a corner table, pitching expansion and a lab-grown “essence” to scale nostalgia. Ana scoffs; cash says yes, pride says no.
  - At Mercado San Cosme and the Serapio Rendón stalls, Ana hunts cheap quelites and amaranth, then rides to Xochimilco. Itzel Xóchitl ferries her down the Cuemanco canal after dark, machete wrapped in cloth, to a protected plot in San Gregorio Atlapulco. Egrets settle; a ritual plot blooms “flor de noche.” Itzel: first-person sliver—“I never teach the canal. I ask it.”
  - Broth of the pollen detonates granular recall in Ana: her father’s aftershave, the crackle of her mother’s comal. Itzel sells her a thumb-sized vial with rules: moon harvest only, never when the canal is closed, never more than a breath. Ana slips microdoses into a dish—charred quelites, amaranth aguachile, a sigh of pollen.
  - Lines form. A Twitter thread calls it “comer recuerdos.” Diners speak dates and rooms with impossible specificity. Carmen, at Ana’s Doctores walk-up, drinks a drop, recognizes her daughter, recites a long-lost salsa ratio near-verbatim, then fogs. Mikel returns, revises: “a memory engine.”
  - Valeria Chen at UNAM’s Instituto de Química tastes, frowns, files a permit map in her tidy lab; warns Cofepris will ask for toxicology. Brownouts ripple; water rations tighten; occasional canal closures after contamination alerts flash on radio.

Act II)
  - Demand crushes Morada. Mateo sleeps on a cot; Ana keeps a grease-stained ledger of who gets a memory and who gets a seat. A guest sobs from a recalled accident; another laughs at a grandmother’s kite. Not all recall is tender. Inspector Luis Aranda appears with a laminated checklist; he refuses a taste. He flags labeling and cold-chain breaks; gives a stern grace period.
  - Interlude—Itzel, first person: “The egrets write the hours. When men write the hours, birds leave.”
  - Diego circles with contracts: ghost-kitchen rollout, a biotech partner, and licensing. He hides a dropout past in botany; he wants Valeria to backstop safety, InDRE in Tlalpan to clear contaminants, Cofepris in Nápoles to stamp an exemption. Valeria agrees to characterize compounds if community consent governs use. Diego pockets a vial when Ana isn’t looking.
  - Night harvests intensify. A rainstorm turns canals ink-black. On a closure night, desperate, Ana breaks the pact and harvests without egrets. Next service the dish goes… dull. Memories smear, unstick. A diner seizes—not from pollen, InDRE later finds, but from an adulterant in city water. Still, Cofepris orders a temporary halt pending process review.
  - Morada goes dim. Ana runs a clandestine candlelit tasting to keep staff fed. Carmen’s clinic bills pile up; her lucid flashes shorten. At San Rafael markets, Ana trades last cash for black cacao and chilhuacle seeds; smell therapy for Carmen. Mateo rides his beat-up Italika to deliver care packages to regulars who can’t afford a table.
  - Mikel publishes a data-heavy piece on recall variability; he questions the ethics of selling memory without a safety net or consent protocols. Tourists swamp Xochimilco anyway; a viral vlog shows Itzel’s chinampa without naming her, but the route is obvious.
  - Interlude—Itzel: “Agreements are not contracts. They are breaths. You break one, the next is shorter.”
  - Valeria detects a fragile aromatic cluster in the pollen—heat-labile, solvent-shy. Scaling will break it. Diego pushes a synthetic analog and a patent filing. He name-drops a venture lab; Ana imagines a memory empire and feels sick.
  - Inspector Aranda raids cleanly. He finds Diego’s pilfered sample logged for export. He shuts Morada for 10 days and opens a file on the supply chain. He does not take Ana’s offered coffee.
